title: A Study to Assess utiLity of BIoEP as an Early Prognostic Indicator for Predicting Anti-Seizure Medication (ASM) Efficacy
official: A Prospective Observational Clinical Study to Investigate the Association Between BioEP and Self-reported Seizure Control During Anti-seizure Medication (ASM) Titration.
summary: This multisite prospective clinical study is to investigate the relationship between seizure type and frequency with the BioEP result during ASM titration in newly diagnosed patients with epilepsy, and to assess the utility of BioEP as an early prognostic indicator of ASM efficacy
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Adult (age 18 and above) presenting with suspected seizure(s).
* Able to give informed consent.
* Patient has received an initial epilepsy diagnosis at time of presentation, or high clinical suspicion of epilepsy and clinician has recommended a trial of ASMs.
* Patient accepts decision to commence ASM.
* Preferably has an EEG prior to commencing ASMs, otherwise has had an EEG within 1 month (30 days) of commencing ASMs.
* Participants initially managed under watchful waiting who later return to clinic and receive a diagnosis of epilepsy (e.g., following a second seizure or a positive EEG) may be included in the study. To be eligible, they must either have had an EEG performed within the 24 months prior to study inclusion (to serve as a baseline), or undergo an EEG before starting ASMs, or within 1 month (30 days) of commencing ASMs.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Participants unable to tolerate an EEG test so no EEG data were gathered.
* Participants with a known hepatic/renal encephalopathy.
* Patient diagnosed with possible Functional Dissociative Seizures (FDS) and epilepsy (dual diagnosis).
* Participants taking part in another Clinical Trial of an Investigational Medicinal Product (CTIMP) (qualitative/observational studies are acceptable).
* Patient receiving low dose ASMs for other conditions (migraines etc).
* Patients with breaches to the skull (burr holes, metallic or plastic plates, shrapnel), where breach rhythms may occur on the EEG over the site
